property_summary: For any creator address and debt token that are distinct, a Cooler created via CoolerFactory always has owner() equal to the creating address and hence owner() != debt(); the mutant reads the debt-token argument (offset 0x28) as owner(), making owner() == debt() and violating the rule.

For any direct call, C.owner() resolves an immutable-arg offset within the call itself and must therefore never return address(0); the mutant reads an offset beyond the calldata, returning address(0) and violating the rule.

For any Cooler created by CoolerFactory on behalf of a creator distinct from the debt token, owner() must return the creator's address; the mutant reads the debt-token immutable arg instead, so owner() returns the debt address, differing from the creator.

C.owner() must always return the address found at immutable-arg offset 0x0 of the calldata tail (with the 2-byte length suffix), so probing owner() with arbitrary tail calldata returns that first embedded address; the mutant reads offset 0x28 instead and returns a different value whenever the caller supplies distinct embedded addresses.

For any cooler created by CoolerFactory by an actor distinct from the debt token, c.owner() must return the creating actor and hence differ from c.debt(); the mutant reads the debt-token immutable arg as owner, so owner() == debt().

For any crafted clone-style calldata, C.owner() must return the address stored at immutable-arg offset 0x0 (the first appended argument), never the one at offset 0x3c (the factory address); the mutant returns the factory argument instead, which differs whenever the two fuzzed addresses differ.

For any clone-style calldata whose appended immutable args are (owner, collateral, debt, factory) with the 2-byte length trailer, C.owner() must return exactly the first appended argument (offset 0x0, the owner), never the fourth one (offset 0x3c, the factory); the mutant returns the factory argument, which differs whenever owner != factory.
